Study the verses

Every verse in Seed Rush, with its explanation. No timer, no score.

1 / 20Finances & Debt

Proverbs 22:7

The rich rule over the poor, and the borrower is slave to the lender.

Show explanation

The first part of the verse is a reality in most instances. The second part is a warning. The Bible warns us about borrowing money from others, because for as long as we owe them money, we are in debt to them. And debt is something the Bible constantly warns us against. Be very careful who you ask to borrow money from, but ideally, don't find yourself in that situation in the first place.

2 / 20Finances & Debt

Matthew 6:24

No one can serve two masters. Either you will hate the one and love the other, or you will be devoted to the one and despise the other. You cannot serve both God and money.

Show explanation

There is no way to have your heart follow two masters. Your heart will lean towards one, and away from the other. You cannot live as a servant to the money you make (or can make), but that is a temptation that many people easily fall into. They start basing their life around their job, and around the money they'll be able to make if they just complete another job. But Jesus should be the only Master of our lives, and we should make decisions based on what He says, not on what our money "says".

3 / 20Stewardship

Luke 16:11

So if you have not been trustworthy in handling worldly wealth, who will trust you with true riches?

Show explanation

In an incredibly interesting parable from Jesus, we learn that he expects us to be smart about our finances, and in some instances, think outside the box, just like the Shrewd Manager. He doesn't want our finances to just be money we can count… because. He wants us to use our finances to achieve good things, and wants us to make them be fruitful. When we handle the worldly wealth he has given us well, we can rest assured he will trust us with true riches, in this life and in heaven.

Read the full page

4 / 20Stewardship

Matthew 6:19

Do not store up for yourselves treasures on earth, where moths and vermin destroy, and where thieves break in and steal

Show explanation

In this chapter of many teachings, Jesus gives us a clear reality check. The treasures of this world can be easily destroyed and stolen. Not only that, but they're only temporary. Despite that, so many people, Christians included, spend hours upon hours of their day with the main and sole focus of trying to store up earthly treasures, instead of giving focus to the treasures that are eternal.

Read the full page

5 / 20Stewardship

Proverbs 27:23

Be sure you know the condition of your flocks, give careful attention to your herds;

Show explanation

The verse talks about stewardship. Though not as widely known, there are many valuable lessons to be taken from it. With everything that God gives us, he expects us to care for it. It is only when we are attentive to it and intentional with it, that we are able to truly care for it, and treat it with the respect God wants us to treat it with.

Read the full page

6 / 20Growth

Proverbs 13:11

Dishonest money dwindles away, but whoever gathers money little by little makes it grow.

Show explanation

Think about people who try a get-rich-quick scheme, or who try to gamble their money. They all have the hope of winning as much as possible, with as little work as possible, but with an incredibly high risk. The same thing happens to almost all in the end. Their money quickly disappears. The one who has patience to slowly grow financially is different though. Their finances will grow with each and every day.

Read the full page

7 / 20Responsibility

2 Thessalonians 3:10

For even when we were with you, we gave you this rule: “The one who is unwilling to work shall not eat.

Show explanation

The most nightmarish verse for lazy people. This verse follows the logic of one of the most well-known rules of the spiritual world: The law of sowing and reaping. If you are not willing to work, why would you expect that you should eat? God made us to be useful creatures, diligent. There is no use in praying for God to provide to us, if we ourselves are not willing to do the part that is within our reach.

8 / 20Timeliness

Proverbs 6:8

yet it stores its provisions in summer and gathers its food at harvest.

Show explanation

Following the example of the wise ant, this verse explains how the ant wisely gathers its food before winter, because it knows that when winter comes, it will not be able to leave the comfort of its shelter to collect food, and food itself will be scarce. The ant knows that it must work before winter comes, and so, it begins to work, and it works tirelessly.

Read the full page

9 / 20Timeliness

Ecclesiastes 3:1

There is a time for everything, and a season for every activity under the heavens:

Show explanation

This verse provides a great reminder of the natural order of things. There is a season for everything, and nothing lasts forever. The good seasons and the bad seasons, all come and go. As it relates to work and finances, there is a time to plant, and a time to harvest. The time to plant is tiring and hard, but nonetheless, it has its time. The time to harvest is great, and full of joy, but we know that at some point we'll have to begin planting again. In everything, it's important to remember that God has a purpose in every season, and we should aim to do the work that is required of us in that season.

10 / 20Generosity & Giving

Malachi 3:10

Bring the whole tithe into the storehouse, that there may be food in my house. Test me in this,” says the Lord Almighty, “and see if I will not throw open the floodgates of heaven and pour out so much blessing that there will not be room enough to store it

Show explanation

God makes an amazing and generous offer for his people. If they care for his house and honor his request of ensuring there is always food in his house (temple), he will bless those people so much that they will not have enough room to store them. People are often reluctant to give because they fear they won't have enough. If we pay attention to God's promise though, we'll see that giving means ensuring that we will have more than enough, so there's no reason to be afraid.

Read the full page

11 / 20Generosity & Giving

2 Corinthians 9:7

Each of you should give what you have decided in your heart to give, not reluctantly or under compulsion, for God loves a cheerful giver.

Show explanation

The focus of this verse is on your heart, specifically on what the reason you're giving for is. God makes it perfectly clear that he wants his people to give because they find joy in giving, and because they are joyful in the Lord. He doesn't want people giving out of obligation. Whenever you feel like you're giving by force, remember to recenter your heart on Jesus, who was always willing to give what he had with a grateful and joyful heart, not out of obligation.

Read the full page

12 / 20Generosity & Giving

Proverbs 3:9

Honor the Lord with your wealth, with the firstfruits of all your crops;

Show explanation

God makes it abundantly clear throughout all his word that the firstfruits should be reserved to him. The firstfruits refer to the best crops of the field, and he wants his people to honor him with the best that they have. Think about how much God has given you, and about all the amazing grace that he has poured upon you. When we take time to think about that, it starts to become easy to see why God deserves nothing less than our best!

13 / 20Contentment

1 Timothy 6:10

For the love of money is a root of all kinds of evil. Some people, eager for money, have wandered from the faith and pierced themselves with many griefs.

Show explanation

Some people believe that money gives you power. Though it might increase your power to buy things, it diminishes the infinitely more important power: Freedom. Many people live as slaves for their love of money. Many find themselves in a life of sin and corruption, just so they can make more money. In the end, that love of money will surely lead to many unexpected griefs.

Read the full page

14 / 20Contentment

Hebrews 13:5

Keep your lives free from the love of money and be content with what you have, because God has said, “Never will I leave you; never will I forsake you.

Show explanation

A simple verse that at first seems to be talking about unrelated topics. What does the love of money have to do with God not leaving me? The connection here is satisfaction. Those who love money are never satisfied, always wanting more. They believe that maybe if they have more money, they'll find what they're looking for. But God's direct response to that is that his promise to never leave or forsake us is what satisfies. If someone knows and understands that, there is no reason to keep loving money.

Read the full page

15 / 20Work & Diligence

Proverbs 6:6

Go to the ant, you sluggard; consider its ways and be wise!

Show explanation

Solomon uses the ant as an example for being hard working. The ant always works before winter, because it knows that when winter comes, it will not be able to leave the comfort of its shelter to collect food, and food itself will be scarce. The ant knows that it must work before winter comes, and so, it begins to work, and it works tirelessly. In the same way, anyone who is lazy should learn the importance of working to have enough for seasons of difficulty, just like the ant does.

Read the full page

16 / 20Work & Diligence

Colossians 3:23

Whatever you do, work at it with all your heart, as working for the Lord, not for human masters

Show explanation

In all the work we do, God wants us to do it with all our hearts. He does not want us to do it out of obligation, but from a place of love. And this is not only referring to the work we do at church. This is referring to all areas of our life. Finances, sure. But anything as it relates to our job, family, friends, community, and anything else. Do it with love, as if you were doing it for God.

Read the full page

17 / 20Planning & Wisdom

Proverbs 21:5

The plans of the diligent lead to profit as surely as haste leads to poverty.

Show explanation

A diligent person is someone who does the work that needs to be done at the right time. They courageously work on what they set themselves up to do. The one who does that will reap a good reward. Laziness, though, will not lead to those good rewards. The fruit of laziness is actually the opposite: poverty.

Read the full page

18 / 20Planning & Wisdom

Luke 14:28

Suppose one of you wants to build a tower. Won’t you first sit down and estimate the cost to see if you have enough money to complete it?

Show explanation

Jesus gives a serious and honest warning here. A smart person will sit down and make sure they will have enough funds to complete a certain project (building a tower in this case) before they begin, so they can be sure they'll finish it. If they won't have enough, then beginning it will just be a waste of money and time. In the same way, anyone who wants to follow Jesus should sit down and think about the cost that comes with it. And Jesus makes it obvious that the price for it is not small.

Read the full page

19 / 20Planning & Wisdom

Proverbs 16:3

Commit to the Lord whatever you do, and he will establish your plans.

Show explanation

Whatever dreams, goals, and plans you might have for your finances or for any area of your life, the most important thing you can do (and the first thing you should do) is commit them to God. He helps make sure our plans will align with his, and when they are, they will be established in a strong foundation.

Read the full page

20 / 20Trust & Provision

Philippians 4:19

And my God will meet all your needs according to the riches of his glory in Christ Jesus.

Show explanation

Here, Paul talks about a great and comforting promise. God will meet all our needs. Notice that it does not say that God will meet all our wants, or give us every little thing we desire. But peace is found in knowing that God will provide for all of our needs. And if we know we won't lack anything, then why would we be worried about anything?
